We differentiate each component separately.

- For the $x$-component $x(t)=7-3t,$ we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=-3,
$$

and therefore,

$$
{x}^{′}(1)=-3.
$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t)=2{t}^{2},$ we have

$$
{y}^{′}(t)=4t,
$$

and therefore,

$$
{y}^{′}(1)=4(1)=4.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(1) & =⟨{x}^{′}(1),\,{y}^{′}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|{r}^{′}(1)| & =\sqrt{{(-3)}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
